title: QT interval and antidepressant use: a cross sectional study of electronic health records
authors: Castro VM, Clements CC, Murphy SN, Gainer VS, Fava M, Weilburg JB, et al.
population: Adults with an electrocardiogram after prescription of an antidepressant or methadone in a New England healthcare system of two academic medical centres and outpatient clinics, February 1990 to August 2011; 6293 on sertraline
funder: The project was supported by the NIH/National Library of Medicine (award No 2U54LM008748) and the National Institute of Mental Health (award No R01MH086026).
authorConflicts: One author (MF) reported consulting fees or advisory roles for many pharmaceutical companies including Eli Lilly, GlaxoSmithKline, Janssen and Pfizer; RHP reported consulting fees from several companies.
result: Dose-response association with QTc prolongation for citalopram (adjusted beta 0.10, SE 0.04, p<0.01; within-subject mean QTc increase 10.3 ms from 20 to 40 mg), escitalopram and amitriptyline, but not for other antidepressants examined, including sertraline (adjusted beta 0.01, SE 0.01). Cross-sectional design without random assignment.
